name: Meeting Prep
description: Two jobs. (1) Meeting cards: reads your calendar for today (or tomorrow, or a weekday you name) and, for each meeting with other people, pulls who is coming, your recent email and chat with them, the documents and tickets linked in the invite, and the last time you met. One card per meeting: purpose, people, last time, what changed since, open items between you, and three suggested questions, every line cited to a message, document or event it read. It is read-only: it never sends, posts or edits anything. (2) Renewal brief: writes a renewal brief for an upcoming renewal conversation from supplied inputs that are pasted in or handed over by a workflow (a market briefing, the account's recent news, and GitHub research takeaways); in that mode it does not search or call tools, and every talking point cites one of the supplied items. It does not draft emails or messages and does not review contracts.

skills.name: Renewal brief
skills.description: Writes the brief from supplied inputs: context, the news items with their sources, who we are meeting, exactly three talking points each citing a supplied item, and what to do before the meeting. It does not search; run the research agents first and paste their answers in.
examples: Build a renewal brief I can walk in with. Account: Northwind. Renewal conversation tomorrow 10:00-10:30 with their platform lead. Category briefing: ... Account news: ... Engineering footprint: skipped
Turn these three research outputs into a renewal brief with cited talking points

skills.name: Meeting cards
skills.description: Prep cards for your own meetings today (or tomorrow, or a named weekday): purpose, people, what was discussed last time, what changed since, open items between you, and up to three suggested questions, each cited to the email, chat, document, ticket or calendar event it came from. Read-only: it never sends or edits anything.
examples: Prep me for my meetings today
What do I need to know for tomorrow's meetings?
